text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
HELSINGIN SANOMAT

- President Martti Ahtisaari is still the favourite to become Finland's next president with the support of 35 percent of Finns; he was followed with equal 32 percent support by speaker of parliament Speaker Riitta Ousukainen and U.N. human rights' envoy Elisabeth Rehn, a poll by Suomen Gallup shows.
- The Young Finns party re-elected Risto E.J. Penttila party leader at its conference on Sunday. @
- About 40 percent of Finns think parliament should support Finland's membership of European economic and monetary union EMU, while about 38 percent think it should not, a poll shows.
- Norwegian men's and women's teams won Finland's premier orienteering competition, the 49th "Jukola" relay, at the weekend.
KAUPPALEHTI
- Growth of 20-30 percent to the year 2000 is forecast for small electronics companies which work under subcontract to major telecommucations equipment companies, such as Nokia and Ericsson. @

- Finland has good investment opportunities, British investment bank Charterhouse Development Capital's managing director Roger Pilgrim says, adding that the bank is looking for Finnish firms to invest in.
- Dissolving a company will be taxed more heavily and earned income could be taxed as capital income, the finance ministry plans.
- The goal of lowering Finland's high unemployment figures gives good grounds for a moderate pay deal agreement, says Juhana Vartiainen at the Labour Institute of Economic Research. @
- The real-estate business has livened up considerably, even cuts in construction subsidies have not dampened enthusianism, sector representative says.
DEMARI

- New chairman of the Wood and Allied Workers Union says a comprehensive pay deal can be reached in the autumn round of collective bargaining even without the paper workers' union, which has said it will not join a braod deal.
- Prime Minister Paavo Lipponen said his government is ready to discuss the reservations that the Finnish farmers union MTK has about European economic and monetary union, EMU. @
AAMULEHTI
- Buying defence equipment together with Sweden will be an excellent way to save money, President Ahtisaari says.
- The Finnish Meat Industry Federation proposes to reform the meat pricing system in the retail sector to bring it into line with European price flexibility.
TURUN SANOMAT
- Neutrality is the best policy for Finland and Sweden, opposition leader Esko Aho, chairman of the Centre Party, says.
-- Nora Hallberg, Helsinki Newsroom +358-9-680 50 292
